```{r}
add_overlay <- function(..., label = NULL, label_style = NULL) {
  el <- list(...)

  y <- '<div id="overlay-highlight"'
  if(length(el) > 0) {
    y <- c(y, 'style="', glue::glue('{names(el)}:{el};'))
  }
  y <- c(y, '">')

  if(!is.null(label)) {
    y <- c(y, glue::glue('<span" class="vertical-center"" style="{label_style}">{label}</span>'))
  }

  knitr::asis_output(glue::glue_collapse(c(y, "</div>")))
}
```

## The Drift Diffusion Model

- Model of **two-choice** decisions: evidence is **accumulated** over time until it hits one of two **boundaries**
- Explains **what** you respond $\rightarrow$ choice, and **when** $\rightarrow$ response time (RT)

- **Example: flanker task**: "Which way does the middle arrow point?" 
  - evidence accumulates toward **"left"** or **"right"**
  - incongruent flankers $\rightarrow$ lower drift rate $\rightarrow$ slower, more errors

- **Widely used**:
  - decision-making, memory, cognitive control, even creativity
  - as a **measurement tool**, e.g. to validate clinical diagnoses

.footnote[Stone (1960); Link & Heath (1975); Ratcliff (1978) · **Applications:** Krajbich et al. (2010); Starns (2012); White (2011); Donzallaz (2023); Weigard (2021)]


---
class: light

## The 7 DDM Parameters

```{r ddm-pic, fig.width = 10, fig.height = 4, out.width = "100%"}
library(ggplot2)
library(grid)



col_bg    <- "#ebedf0"   
col_fg    <- "#001300"
col_ez    <- "#f88a30"  
col_five  <- "#75b44b"   
col_seven <- "#ea6f82"   

alpha <- 1
tau   <- 0.25

t_knots <- c(0, 0.35, 0.42, 0.75, 1.15, 1.55, 1.75, 2.40, 2.85, 3.30, 3.75, 4.20)
y_knots <- c(tau,  0.12, 0.25, 0.32, 0.18, 0.55, 0.35, 0.62, 0.58, 0.88, 0.70, alpha)


y_knots_scaled <- tau + (y_knots - tau) * 0.62
y_knots_scaled[length(y_knots_scaled)] <- alpha

path_interp <- spline(t_knots, y_knots_scaled, n = 50, method = "natural")
time_path   <- path_interp$x

set.seed(7)
n <- length(time_path)


slow_walk    <- cumsum(rnorm(n, 0, 0.040)) * 0.20
medium_bumps <- cumsum(rnorm(n, 0, 0.07))  * 0.14
spikes       <- rnorm(n, 0, 0.09)

spike_locs <- sample(seq(5, n - 5), size = 6)
spike_dir  <- sample(c(-1, 1), size = 6, replace = TRUE)
spikes[spike_locs] <- spikes[spike_locs] + spike_dir * runif(6, 0.14, 0.22)

jitter <- slow_walk + medium_bumps + spikes
jitter <- jitter - mean(jitter)

ev_path <- path_interp$y + jitter


ev_path <- ev_path - ev_path[1] + tau


hard_cap <- alpha * 0.72
ev_path[1:(n-1)] <- pmin(ev_path[1:(n-1)], hard_cap)


min_val <- 0.04
too_low <- ev_path < min_val
ev_path[too_low] <- min_val + abs(ev_path[too_low] - min_val) * 0.3


blend_start <- round(n * 0.88)
for (i in blend_start:n) {
  w <- ((i - blend_start) / (n - blend_start))^2
  ev_path[i] <- (1 - w) * ev_path[i] + w * alpha
}


ev_path[1] <- tau
ev_path[n] <- alpha

rt <- max(time_path)
df_path <- data.frame(time = time_path, evidence = ev_path)

tau_x1 <- -0.38
tau_x2 <-  0.00
beta_x <- -0.07

left_margin <- -0.95   

x_max <- 5.8
x_min <- left_margin
x     <- seq(x_min, x_max, length.out = 1500)

x_shift    <- pmax(x - 0.0, 0)
top_raw    <- dgamma(x_shift, shape = 5.0, scale = 0.42)
bottom_raw <- dgamma(x_shift, shape = 5.0, scale = 0.42)

top_raw    <- top_raw    / max(top_raw)
bottom_raw <- bottom_raw / max(bottom_raw)

top_raw[x    < 0] <- 0
bottom_raw[x < 0] <- 0

taper <- ifelse(x < rt - 0.3, 1, exp(-((x - (rt - 0.3))^2) / (2 * 0.15^2)))
taper[x >= rt] <- 0

top_raw    <- top_raw    * taper
bottom_raw <- bottom_raw * taper

top_raw[top_raw       < 0.002] <- 0
bottom_raw[bottom_raw < 0.002] <- 0

top_y    <-  alpha + top_raw    * 0.44
bottom_y <- -bottom_raw         * 0.22

df_dens <- data.frame(x = x, top_y = top_y, bottom_y = bottom_y)


arr_x1 <- 1.6;  arr_y1 <- 0.08
arr_x2 <- 2.3;  arr_y2 <- 0.32
offset <- 0.10


sv_fan <- data.frame(
  x    = c(arr_x1, arr_x1),
  xend = c(arr_x1 + 0.65, arr_x1 + 0.65),
  y    = c(arr_y1, arr_y1),
  yend = c(arr_y1 + 0.62, arr_y1 + 0.12)
)


sw_x     <- -0.72          
sw_half  <- 0.095          


st0_y     <- -0.16
st0_x1    <- tau_x1
st0_x2    <- 0.02
st0_xmid  <- (st0_x1 + st0_x2) / 2

p <- ggplot() +
  
    geom_ribbon(data = df_dens,
              aes(x = x, ymin = alpha, ymax = top_y),
              fill = "#5c6b58", colour = col_fg, linewidth = 0.4) +
  
  geom_ribbon(data = df_dens,
              aes(x = x, ymin = bottom_y, ymax = 0),
              fill = "#5c6b58", colour = col_fg, linewidth = 0.4) +
  
  geom_segment(aes(x = left_margin, xend = x_max, y = alpha, yend = alpha),
               colour = col_fg, linewidth = 1.2) +
  geom_segment(aes(x = left_margin, xend = x_max, y = 0, yend = 0),
               colour = col_fg, linewidth = 1.2) +
  geom_segment(aes(x = 0, xend = 0, y = -0.05, yend = alpha + 0.05),
               colour = col_fg, linewidth = 1.2) +
  
  # tau 
  geom_segment(aes(x = tau_x1, xend = tau_x2, y = tau, yend = tau),
               colour = col_ez, linewidth = 1.3) +
  geom_segment(aes(x = tau_x1, xend = tau_x1, y = tau - 0.04, yend = tau + 0.04),
               colour = col_ez, linewidth = 1.0) +
  
  # s_tau 
  geom_segment(aes(x = st0_x1, xend = st0_x2, y = st0_y, yend = st0_y),
               colour = col_seven, linewidth = 2.2, alpha = 0.35, lineend = "round") +
  geom_segment(aes(x = st0_x1, xend = st0_x1, y = st0_y - 0.035, yend = st0_y + 0.035),
               colour = col_seven, linewidth = 1.0) +
  geom_segment(aes(x = st0_x2, xend = st0_x2, y = st0_y - 0.035, yend = st0_y + 0.035),
               colour = col_seven, linewidth = 1.0) +
  
  # beta 
  geom_segment(aes(x = beta_x, xend = beta_x, y = 0.01, yend = tau - 0.01),
               colour = col_five, linewidth = 1.3,
               arrow = arrow(ends = "both", length = unit(0.10, "inches"),
                             type = "closed")) +
  
  # s_beta 
  geom_segment(aes(x = sw_x, xend = sw_x, y = tau - sw_half, yend = tau + sw_half),
               colour = col_seven, linewidth = 2.2, alpha = 0.35, lineend = "round") +
  geom_segment(aes(x = sw_x - 0.08, xend = sw_x + 0.08, y = tau - sw_half, yend = tau - sw_half),
               colour = col_seven, linewidth = 1.0) +
  geom_segment(aes(x = sw_x - 0.08, xend = sw_x + 0.08, y = tau + sw_half, yend = tau + sw_half),
               colour = col_seven, linewidth = 1.0) +
  
  geom_line(data = df_path, aes(x = time, y = evidence),
            colour = col_fg, linewidth = 1.2) +
  
  geom_segment(aes(x = rt, xend = rt, y = alpha, yend = alpha + 0.06),
               colour = "#001300", linewidth = 1.2) +
  
  # nu 
  geom_segment(aes(x = arr_x1, xend = arr_x2, y = arr_y1, yend = arr_y2),
               colour = col_ez, linewidth = 1.4,
               arrow = arrow(length = unit(0.12, "inches"), type = "closed")) +
  
  # s_nu 
  geom_segment(data = sv_fan, aes(x = x, xend = xend, y = y, yend = yend),
               colour = col_five, linewidth = 1.2, alpha = 0.85,
               arrow = arrow(length = unit(0.10, "inches"), type = "closed")) +
  
  annotate("text", x = tau_x1 + 0.20, y = alpha + 0.07,
           label = expression(alpha), colour = col_ez,
           size = 7, hjust = -0.2, vjust = 0.9) +
  
  annotate("text", x = (tau_x1 + tau_x2) / 2, y = tau + 0.05,
           label = expression(tau), colour = col_ez,
           size = 6, hjust = 0.5) +
  
  annotate("text", x = arr_x1 + 0.90, y = arr_y1 + 0.2 ,
           label = expression(nu), colour = col_ez, size = 6, hjust = 1, vjust = 1) +
  
  annotate("text", x = beta_x - 0.11, y = tau / 2,
           label = expression(beta), colour = col_five,
           size = 6, hjust = 1, vjust = 0.5) +
  
  annotate("text", x = arr_x1 + 0.65, y = arr_y1 + 0.72,
           label = expression(s[nu]), colour = col_five, size = 6, hjust = 0.5, fontface = "bold") +
  
  annotate("text", x = sw_x - 0.10, y = tau,
           label = expression(s[beta]), colour = col_seven,
           size = 6, hjust = 1, vjust = 0.5) +
  
  annotate("text", x = st0_xmid, y = st0_y - 0.10,
           label = expression(s[tau]), colour = col_seven,
           size = 6, hjust = 0.5) +
  
  annotate("text", x = rt + 0.12, y = alpha + 0.11,
           label = "observed RT", colour = "#001300",
           size = 4.5, hjust = 0.0) +
  
  annotate("text", x = x_max - 0.1, y = alpha - offset,
           label = "correct bound", colour = col_fg,
           size = 4.5, hjust = 1) +
  
  annotate("text", x = x_max - 0.1, y = 0 + offset,
           label = "error bound", colour = col_fg,
           size = 4.5, hjust = 1) +
  
  annotate("text", x = left_margin + 0.10, y = 0.62,
           label = "evidence", colour = col_fg,
           angle = 90, size = 5.5) +
  
  annotate("text", x = -0.02, y = 0.00,
           label = "0", colour = col_fg, size = 5.5, hjust = 1.2, vjust = 1.2) +
  
  coord_cartesian(
    xlim = c(left_margin, x_max),
    ylim = c(-0.42, 1.36),
    clip = "off"
  ) +
  
  theme_void() +
  theme(plot.background = element_rect(fill = col_bg, colour = NA))

p
```

class: light

## Weak Spots of the DDM

- **Estimation** is difficult:
  - identifiability issues
  - computational complexity
  - long computing times
- $\rightarrow$ hard for many researchers to use


- **Solutions**:
  - better estimation techniques
  - efficient approximations
  - reduced complexity $\rightarrow$ .c4[EZ-DDM]

.footnote[Boehm (2018); Henrich (2024); Lüken (2025) · **EZ:** Wagenmakers et al. (2007)]

---
class: light

## Hierarchical DDMs

- **Fitting each participant separately**:
  - $\rightarrow$ overestimates individual differences
  - noise is read as true variability
  
  
- **Hierarchical models** add a second level:
  - individual parameters are drawn from a **population distribution**
  - $\rightarrow$ inference on the **individual and group level** at the same time

.footnote[Rouder et al. (2017); Boehm et al. (2018); Lee (2011); Vandekerckhove et al. (2011)]

---
class: light

## Why Hierarchical Modelling?

- **Advantages**:
  - reliable estimates even with **sparse data** per participant
  - parameters can vary **selectively** (some fixed, some free) $\rightarrow$ no overly complex models
- Hierarchical versions exist for many cognitive models, e.g. MPT models and the DDM


- **Bayesian modelling**:
  - $\rightarrow$ makes complex models tractable
  - frequentist hierarchical estimation is much harder

.footnote[Lee (2011); Vandekerckhove et al. (2011); Smith & Batchelder (2010); Rouder & Lu (2005)]
---

class: pink-light


# The EZ Diffusion Model

- Developed by Wagenmakers et al. (2007) as a **frequentist**, **non-hierarchical** model
- Estimates **3 key parameters**: drift rate $\nu$, boundary separation $\alpha$, non-decision time $\tau$
- Simplifying assumptions:
  - no a priori bias $\rightarrow$ $\beta = \frac{\alpha}{2}$
  - no across-trial variability in $\nu$, $\beta$ and $\tau$
- Computed from **3 summary statistics**:
  - mean of the correct RTs ($MRT$)
  - variance of the correct RTs ($VRT$)
  - accuracy, i.e. proportion correct ($Pc$)

.footnote[Wagenmakers et al. (2007)]


---
class: pink-light

# Why use the EZ DDM?

- **Computationally easy**: computes 3 parameters per condition and participant
- **Surprisingly robust**:
  - stable even with very low error rates, where full DDM fits can become unreliable or fail to converge
  - based on aggregated measures $\rightarrow$ less sensitive to RT outliers
- **Hierarchical EZ-DDM**:
  - handles individual differences in a principled way
  - $\rightarrow$ more stable estimates than fitting each participant separately

.footnote[Wagenmakers et al. (2007); Chávez De la Peña & Vandekerckhove (2025); Lee (2011); Vandekerckhove et al. (2011)]

---
class: pink-light 

## The Hierarchical EZ-DDM

Choice and RT of person $i$ on trial $j$ follow a Wiener distribution:

$$\mathbf{Y}_{ij} \sim \text{Wiener}(\alpha_i, \beta_i, \tau_i, \nu_i), \quad \beta_i = \frac{\alpha_i}{2}$$

**EZ:** instead of this likelihood, the parameters are linked to the data through **3 summary statistics**:

$$MRT_i \sim \text{Normal}\left(M_{ci}, \frac{\Sigma_{ci}}{C_i}\right)$$

$$VRT_i \sim \text{Normal}\left(\Sigma_{ci}, \frac{2\Sigma_{ci}^2}{C_i - 1}\right) \quad (C_i > 30)$$

.footnote[Chávez De la Peña & Vandekerckhove (2025)]
---

class: pink-light

The Normal is a large-sample approximation, the sampling distribution later used in our Stan model is

$$VRT_i \sim \text{Gamma}\left(\frac{C_i - 1}{2}, \frac{C_i - 1}{2\Sigma_{ci}}\right)$$

$$C_i \sim \text{Binomial}(\pi_{ci}, J)$$


---
class: pink-light

## Linking to the DDM Parameters

Mean of the correct RTs:

$$M_{ci} = \tau_i + \frac{\alpha_i}{2\nu_i} \cdot \frac{u_i - 1}{u_i + 1}$$

Variance of the correct RTs:

$$\Sigma_{ci} = \frac{\alpha_i}{2\nu_i^3} \cdot \frac{1 - 2\alpha_i\nu_i u_i - u_i^2}{(u_i + 1)^2}$$

Probability of a correct response:

$$\pi_{ci} = \frac{1}{\exp(-\alpha_i\nu_i) + 1}$$

with $u_i = \exp(-\alpha_i \nu_i)$

---

# Parameter Recovery

- Simulation: Lexical Decision
- **100 participants × 300 trials**, 10 simulated data sets
- 4 cells per person: nonwords (150 trials), high-, low- and very-low-frequency words (50 each)
- **Drift rate** depends on word vs. nonword and on word frequency
- **Boundary separation** and **non-decision time**: one value per person
- All person-level parameters vary between participants
- No bias, no across-trial variability $\rightarrow$ the data meet the EZ assumptions

.footnote[Parameter values based on Ratcliff, Gomez & McKoon (2004); data simulated with `rtdists::rdiffusion()`]

---

class: pink-light

## The Fitted Model

Cell $k$ of person $i$:

$$\nu_{ik} = \nu_{0i} + \nu_{1i}\, c_{1k} + \nu_{2i}\, c_{2k} \qquad \alpha_{ik} = \exp(\alpha_i) \qquad \tau_{ik} = \tau_i$$

Each person-level parameter comes from a population distribution:

$$\theta_i \sim \text{Normal}(\mu_\theta, \sigma_\theta)$$

- $c_{1k}$: +1 nonword, −1 word
- $c_{2k}$: centred word frequency
- small cell-level deviations for $\nu$, $\alpha$ and $\tau$
- Stan (cmdstanr): 4 chains, 1000 warm-up + 1000 samples
- Across all 10 fits: `r sum(res$diag$divergences)` divergent transitions, max $\hat{R}$ = `r round(max(res$diag$max_rhat), 3)`

---

class: pink-light

## Population Level

```{r rec-pop, fig.width = 10, fig.height = 4.6, out.width = "100%"}
res$pop %>%
  mutate(par = factor(par, levels = names(pop_labels), labels = pop_labels)) %>%
  ggplot(aes(x = factor(rep), y = est)) +
  geom_hline(aes(yintercept = true), linetype = 2, colour = truth_col, linewidth = 0.8) +
  geom_pointrange(aes(ymin = lo, ymax = hi), size = 0.25, colour = "#001300") +
  facet_wrap(~ par, scales = "free_y", ncol = 5) +
  scale_x_discrete(breaks = c(1, 5, 10)) +
  labs(x = "simulated data set", y = "posterior mean [95% CrI]") +
  theme_light_slide(13)
```

.small[
- **Population means**: true value inside the 95% CrI in almost all data sets
- **Between-person SDs of the effects** (word/nonword, frequency): wide intervals $\rightarrow$ they tend to be underestimated
]

```{r rec-sub, fig.width = 10, fig.height = 3.4, out.width = "100%"}
  geom_abline(linetype = 2, colour = truth_col, linewidth = 0.8) +
  geom_point(alpha = 0.5, size = 1.4, colour = "#001300") +
  facet_wrap(~ par, scales = "free", ncol = 5) +
  labs(x = "true", y = "posterior mean") +
  theme_light_slide(13)
```

.small[
- One simulated data set (`r length(unique(res$sub$subj))` participants)
- **Intercepts** recovered well: $\tau$ (r = `r r_sub[["tau_s"]]`), $\nu$ (r = `r r_sub[["nu_intercept_s"]]`), $\alpha$ (r = `r r_sub[["alpha_s"]]`)
- **Individual effects** (word/nonword: r = `r r_sub[["nu_c_s"]]`, frequency: r = `r r_sub[["nu_c2_s"]]`): strong shrinkage toward the group mean
- $\rightarrow$ small true differences between people (SD = 0.15) are hard to detect from 4 cells per person
]

---

class: pink-light

## Cell Level

```{r rec-cell, fig.width = 10, fig.height = 3.8, out.width = "100%"}
res$cell %>%
  mutate(par = factor(par, levels = names(cell_labels), labels = cell_labels)) %>%
  ggplot(aes(true, est, colour = cell)) +
  geom_abline(linetype = 2, colour = "grey40", linewidth = 0.8) +
  geom_point(alpha = 0.3, size = 0.8) +
  facet_wrap(~ par, scales = "free") +
  scale_colour_manual(values = cell_cols) +
  guides(colour = guide_legend(override.aes = list(alpha = 1, size = 3))) +
  labs(x = "true", y = "posterior mean", colour = NULL) +
  theme_light_slide(13)
```

.small[
- $\tau$ well (r = `r r_cell[["t0"]]`), $\nu$ good (r = `r r_cell[["v"]]`), $\alpha$ noisier (r = `r r_cell[["a"]]`)
- Frequency effect is visible: high-frequency words have the highest drift rates
]
